$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.
goal: one sentence, in the user's words
status: scouting | planning | awaiting-approval | building | reviewing | integrating | done | blocked

scout.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string scout
facts: verified statements about what exists today, each with a file:line
unknowns: questions the plan must answer or assume

architect.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string architect
architect.rationale: why this shape and not the cheaper one

s1.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string builder, never orchestrator
s1.branch: written by the builder: the branch this slice's work landed on, or an empty string when the target is not a git repo at all
s1.gate_results: optional: this slice's done_when commands paired with their actual output, when worth keeping verbatim
s1.deviation_from_approved_plan: optional: set only when the orchestrator authorized work outside the architect's approved file set or intent for this slice, and why

s1.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string reviewer, never the builder it is reviewing
s1.summary: optional: one paragraph a human can read without opening findings[]

integrator.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string integrator
integrator.verification: what command proved it works, and its output

ops.written_by: the node that wrote this key - here, always the string ops

log: append-only: node, what it did, timestamp
